verdict.rationale: Sill runs entirely on the user's own devices with no account or vendor server. The Mac host can be built from source with SwiftPM and signed with your own identity, or run from the command line as SillHost. Remote access goes through the user's own VPN or a forwarded port rather than a vendor relay. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license statement and independent hands-on corroboration of building and self-running from source.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
This builds Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development identity, replaces /Applications/Sill.app and opens it.
`swift run -c release SillHost` runs the same host on the command line
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
